sources.quote: Spending per health care provider (HCP), including tax and gratuity, cannot exceed $125.
sources.searcher_note: Describes company dinner guidelines with a $125 per-HCP ceiling; explains the cap but reports no count of Open Payments meals at or just under $125. Page gives month only (August 2015).

sources.quote: In 2017, Pharma Forum released data from 41 pharmaceutical companies that showed the average HCP meal cap was $61 for breakfast, $70 for lunch and $125 for dinner.
sources.searcher_note: Industry survey: $125 is the average company dinner cap; policy, not Open Payments record counts. Page shows modified 2019-10-21.

sources.quote: 50% of organizations set out-of-office dinner limits between $130 and $150 per person.
sources.searcher_note: 2026 compliance survey: half of companies now cap dinners at $130-$150, i.e. above $125; date is the page's dateModified (no publish date shown). Vendor survey, respondent count not given. Different window from the lead's 2024.

sources.quote: The value of meals provided is determined by dividing the total cost of the meal by the total number of participants of the meal.
sources.searcher_note: AstraZeneca's own method for the per-person meal value it reports to CMS; names AstraZeneca but gives no cap and says nothing about $125 bunching.

notes: No source found reporting that Open Payments meal records bunch at exactly $125.00 (or $124.99), and none giving the 47,607 / 675 counts or the AstraZeneca vs Pfizer per-1,000 rates. Sources only establish that $125 is a common self-imposed company dinner cap (not a law), matching the lead's own caveat. A JAMA Health Forum 2024 event-level Open Payments study (Grundy et al., PMC11214116) was checked: it bins dinners at $30 to under $150 per person and does not mention $125, so not recorded. Novartis sham-speaker coverage cites far larger per-person dinners but no $125 cap was found on the pages checked. No coverage after 2026-06-30 beyond the vendor survey.
